You are a participant in a laboratory social interaction study. You briefly met the other participant(s), who are same-sex strangers, and now sit in separate cubicles communicating through a computer network. There are two parts, both contributing to your eventual payment. In Part 1, a total of 10 Chinese yuan (CNY) will be divided between you and another person. Two sealed envelopes, A and B, each contain a possible allocation. Neither person knows either allocation. You were told that registration order makes the other person the allocator and you the receiver. The allocator selects a procedure: a coin toss (heads selects envelope A, tails selects B), or personally choosing one of the two sealed envelopes. You are told which procedure the allocator selected, but neither the selected envelope nor its monetary allocation is disclosed at this point. The envelope will be opened after both parts. You are now answering about the allocation procedure, before the instructions and choices for Part 2. Give your own assessment, without assuming the allocation hidden in either envelope.

Select a single integer from 1 to 5: 1=very unfair; 2=a little unfair; 3=neutral; 4=a little fair; 5=very fair. Respond with only the integer.

Your background: 22 years old, female. You are the receiver in Part 1. The allocator selected the procedure of personally selecting a sealed envelope.
To what extent do you think the allocation procedure selected by the allocator is fair?
